title: Discriminant of the Depressed Cubic
description: Formalizes the discriminant Δ = -4p³ - 27q² of the depressed cubic x³ + px + q = 0 and proves it equals the squared product of root differences (x₁-x₂)²(x₁-x₃)²(x₂-x₃)².

overview.historicalContext: The discriminant of a polynomial is one of the most important invariants in algebra. For the depressed cubic x³ + px + q = 0, the discriminant Δ = -4p³ - 27q² determines the nature of the roots: when Δ > 0 all three roots are real and distinct, when Δ = 0 there is a repeated root, and when Δ < 0 one root is real and two are complex conjugates. The formula relates root separation (how far apart roots are) to coefficient data.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the discriminant Δ = -4p³ - 27q² of the depressed cubic x³ + px + q = 0 and prove it equals (x₁-x₂)²(x₁-x₃)²(x₂-x₃)², relating root separation to coefficient data.
overview.text: Discriminant of the depressed cubic: Δ = -4p³ - 27q² = (x₁-x₂)²(x₁-x₃)²(x₂-x₃)²
overview.proofStrategy: The proof uses the Cardano root expressions x₁ = u+v, x₂ = ωu+ω²v, x₃ = ω²u+ωv. Key steps: (1) Prove (x₁-x₂)(x₁-x₃) = 3(u²+uv+v²) using (1-ω)(1-ω²) = 3. (2) Prove (x₂-x₃)² = -3(u-v)² using (ω-ω²)² = -3. (3) Combine to get Δ = -27(u³-v³)². (4) Express (u³-v³)² = q² + 4p³/27 using Cardano conditions. (5) Final: Δ = -4p³ - 27q².
keyInsights: The identity (1-ω)(1-ω²) = 3 (where ω is a primitive cube root of unity) is the key that makes root differences expressible in terms of u² + uv + v²
The factorization (u²+uv+v²)(u-v) = u³-v³ converts squared root products into cubes of the Cardano parameters
The discriminant Δ = -27(u³-v³)² provides a clean intermediate form between roots and coefficients
The identity (u³-v³)² = (u³+v³)² - 4(uv)³ connects to the Cardano conditions u³+v³ = -q and uv = -p/3

sections.title: Cube Root of Unity
sections.summary: Defines ω = e^(2πi/3) and proves ω³ = 1, ω ≠ 1, 1+ω+ω² = 0, ω⁴ = ω.
sections.mathContext: Establishes the algebraic properties of the primitive cube root of unity ω = e^{2\pi i/3}.

sections.title: Root Definitions
sections.summary: Defines the three Cardano roots x₁ = u+v, x₂ = ωu+ω²v, x₃ = ω²u+ωv.
sections.mathContext: The three Cardano roots of x³ + px + q = 0.

sections.title: Root Difference Expressions
sections.summary: Expresses root differences in terms of u, v, ω.
sections.mathContext: Verified: Root differences expressed as linear combinations in u, v with ω coefficients.

sections.title: Main Discriminant Identity
sections.summary: Proves Δ = -27(u³-v³)² and the full identity Δ = -4p³ - 27q².
sections.mathContext: Verified: The discriminant identity connecting root separation to coefficient data.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.summary: Derives that Δ ≠ 0 iff all roots are distinct, and Δ = 0 iff repeated roots.
sections.mathContext: Verified: Characterization of root multiplicity via the discriminant.

conclusion.summary: Complete formalization of the discriminant identity for the depressed cubic. The discriminant Δ = -4p³ - 27q² equals the squared product of root differences, connecting algebraic coefficient data to geometric root separation.
conclusion.implications: This result is fundamental for determining when cubic equations have repeated roots, for computing Galois groups, and for the classification of cubic curves.
openQuestions: Generalize to the full cubic ax³ + bx² + cx + d with Tschirnhaus transformation
